**Other information:**

The value-menu trigger is a native sibling of the header button, so the trigger's `contextmenu` event path never carries the `neo-grid-menu-enabled` class that `Neo.main.DomEvents` registers as a `contextmenu` prevent-default target. A right-click on the arrow therefore opened the browser's own context menu on top of the value menu.

The fix registers `neo-grid-menu-trigger` next to the header's class. The value menu keeps opening exactly as before: the plugin's `contextmenu` listener sits on the wrapper, so the arrow's event still reaches it.

`test/playwright/e2e/grid/IssuesShowcase.spec.mjs` covers it in the engine tier (no Neural Link): a right-click on the arrow produces a `defaultPrevented` contextmenu event and the value menu is open.

**Red first, as asked:**

```
$ npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs \
      test/playwright/e2e/grid/IssuesShowcase.spec.mjs --grep 19952

# on dev (without this change)
Error: expect(received).toEqual(expected)
  Expected: {"prevented": true,  "trusted": true}
  Received: {"prevented": false, "trusted": true}

# on this branch
1 passed (chromium)
```

The whole spec file is green with the change: `9 passed`.

About the second half of the root cause — which component ids an event path carries when it starts on the arrow. The trigger is its own component (`me.trigger`), and the path of a right-click on the arrow is:

```
.neo-grid-menu-trigger (button#neo-grid-header-button-2__trigger)
  → .neo-grid-menu-wrapper (div#neo-grid-header-button-2__wrapper)
```

The plugin's `contextmenu` listener is registered on the owner, whose element is that wrapper, so the event reaches `me.onContextMenu()` and the value menu opens — the browser menu was the only thing showing up. The header button's own path (`button#neo-grid-header-button-2`) carries `neo-grid-menu-enabled`, which is why the header click was already prevented.

Local run note: the pinned `chrome` channel is not available on my machine, so the run above used the bundled Chromium via a local-only config override; the committed config is untouched.
